thingsToDo.title: Explore Dry Tortugas National Park
thingsToDo.description: Dry Tortugas National Park is located about 70 miles west of Key West and was established as a national park in 1992, succeeding earlier monument status. The park covers roughly 100 square miles, most of it open water in the Gulf of Mexico, and includes seven small islands in the lower Florida Keys chain. Fort Jefferson, a massive 19th-century coastal fort begun in 1846, is the best-known historic structure within the park and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Because access is primarily by boat or seaplane, the site preserves a remote maritime setting where military history, coral reef ecosystems, and seabird habitat are documented in the same protected unit.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Key West?
faq.a: Two to three days is enough for core Key West highlights plus one or two local experiences.

faq.q: Should I book tours ahead in Key West?
